practice.title: Local histories in public view
practice.note: Olga works with artists, museums, and researchers to bring local histories into public view through exhibitions, writing, and long-term collaborations.

about.title: From the Kola Peninsula to Lyon
about.introduction: Olga Shirokostup is an independent curator, researcher, and educator. Born in Severomorsk, she works across the European High North and is based in Lyon.
paragraphs: Olga studied history at the Moscow School of Social and Economic Sciences and graduated from the Chto Delat’ School of Engaged Art. Her work moves between long-term institutional collaborations and independent research.

She is currently a curator within the European research project ARCA (Biocultural Heritage in Arctic Cities as a Potential Resource for Climate Adaptation, 2024–2027). She was co-curator of Arctic Art Forum V at the Natural History Museum in Oslo in 2026 and has been part of the Women in the North project, curated by Maria Lind, since 2022.

Between 2021 and 2023, Olga served as Chief Curator of the Radiance Centre for Contemporary Art in Apatity. Since 2023, she has curated the Archive of Artistic Life in Zapolyarye within RAAN. From 2020 to 2024, she was a Research Course Leader at Garage Academy. She is a recipient of a Robert Bosch Stiftung grant and a former participant in the Frame Curatorial Exchange Programme.

projects.title: Women in the North
projects.description: At Kin Museum of Contemporary Art, Olga contributes archival research, essays, exhibitions, and zines to Women in the North, a long-term project curated by Maria Lind. Her contributions include The Warmth of the Invisible Sun, a publication devoted to Evgenia Patsia and the Kola North.

projects.title: Archive of Artistic Life in Zapolyarye
projects.description: An independent archive of contemporary art in Murmansk Oblast, launched by Olga within the Russian Art Archive Network. Beginning with the art scene in Apatity, it brings together testimonies, artworks, documents, and research spanning the mid-1970s through the 2000s.

projects.title: Arctic Art Forum V
projects.description: Co-curated with Ekaterina Sharova at the Natural History Museum in Oslo. The exhibition Climate Microchanges brought artists, researchers, local voices, and Indigenous knowledge into a shared space for thinking about cultural and ecological change in the North.
